数学基础

导数与瞬时变化率

可微函数的导数是瞬时变化率，也是切线斜率。位置对时间的导数是带方向的速度，速度对时间的导数是加速度。

f′(t) = lim Δf/Δt

1 / 表示方式
导数与瞬时变化率 → 描述运动的变化率 → 简谐振动

本振子的可微位置 x(t) 给出 v=dx/dt、a=dv/dt；有方向的速度可以为负，速率是 |v|。微分描述运动，不是产生运动的物理原因。

验证一条关系 · 数学 → 物理

从切线斜率，到物块净力
收起实验

沿用同一个理想弹簧运动和时钟。位置的斜率是带方向的速度；速度的斜率是加速度。牛顿定律把加速度与合外力联系起来。取向右为正；速率是 |v|，不会为负。

斜率与净力
有符号面积与路程
求两次导数，仍是同一场运动

两个橙色探针共享以秒计的时刻。绿线是解析切线，不是实测：第一图为 x(t₀)+v(t₀)Δt，第二图为 v(t₀)+a(t₀)Δt。屏幕夹角还取决于坐标比例，要按实际单位读斜率。

净力与牛顿定律

v = dx/dt，速率 = |v|，a = dv/dt，ΣF = m a = −k x

先比较前两个快照：加速度都为负，但一个速率增大、另一个减小。再比较转向点和过平衡点。下方原有相位、播放控件同时操控两种视图。

向右，速率减少

横轴是两个周期内的秒数；纵轴位置 x，固定 ±1m。虚线为完整预测，青线为已走过部分，绿线为局部切线，橙点为此刻。
速度 v(t) · 切线斜率是 a
横轴是同样的秒数；纵轴是速度 v（m/s）。标尺只随参数组改变，不随相位改变；看清刻度再比较大小。切线斜率单位为 m/s²。

转向点：此刻速度和速率为零，加速度与净力却不为零。v=0 时不要套用 v·a 符号判断速率变化的规则。

对象是物块。竖直支持力与重力抵消；水平无摩擦、无驱动，故 ΣF=−kx=ma。换成其他系统，必须先把全部外力相加再用牛顿定律。理想解析解以这些力学规律为假设；动画不是对真实力的测量或独立证明。

lab.text:
验证一条关系 · 数学 → 物理

一个投影，一个弹簧，同一个相位
收起实验

几何中的圆，为什么能描述真实模型中的弹簧？圆提供运动的函数形状；弹簧的回复力和物块质量决定快慢。从右端静止释放：x(0)=A，v(0)=0。

圆周投影
斜率与净力
有符号面积与路程
01
单位圆
02
正弦与余弦
03
简谐振动

1 · 几何给出一个坐标
q = cos θ, x = A q
q 是半径为 1 的单位圆上无量纲的横坐标。乘以振幅 A，才得到以米计的位移。

2 · 物理定律决定快慢
m x″ = −k x → ω = √(k/m)
牛顿定律和胡克定律给出 x″=−(k/m)x；余弦函数满足 x″=−ω²x，故 ω²=k/m。

3 · 描述同一个 x
x(t) = A cos(ωt), T = 2π/ω
θ=ωt 是相位，以弧度记录进度，一周为 2π。周期 T 是完成一次往返所需的秒数；余弦也是平移相位后的正弦。

先拖到 ¼ 周期：两幅图的横向位置都为零。再保持 k 不变，把 m 加倍：周期变为原来的 √2 倍。改变 A：位移幅度可见地改变，理想周期却不变。

几何 · 单位圆
青点：辅助圆周运动；橙点：q=cosθ。把 q 乘以 A 才是物块位置。物块本身不绕圆转。
物理 · 水平弹簧
位置标尺固定为 −1 至 +1m，改变 A 能看见幅度改变。力箭头只表示方向，大小见下方读数。
连接 · 同一位移随时间变化
横轴是时间 t（秒），纵轴是位移 x（米），范围固定 ±1m。虚线：模型预测；青线：该预测中已走过的部分，不是实测数据。

One projection, one spring, one shared phase
Close experiment

How can a geometric circle describe a physical spring? The circle supplies the shape of the motion; the spring force and mass set its speed. Start at the right-hand extreme, released from rest: x(0)=A, v(0)=0.

q = cos θ, x = A q
q is the dimensionless horizontal coordinate on a radius-1 circle. Amplitude A scales it into metres.

2 · The force law sets the rate
m x″ = −k x → ω = √(k/m)
Newton’s law and Hooke’s law give x″=−(k/m)x. A cosine has x″=−ω²x, so ω²=k/m.

x(t) = A cos(ωt), T = 2π/ω
θ=ωt is phase in radians; one turn is 2π. T is the time in seconds for one oscillation. Cosine is a phase-shifted sine.

nodes.title: Buck converter

nodes.description: Vary switch ON time within a fixed period. Duty is the fraction of the period spent ON.

nodes.title: Boost converter

lab.text:
TRY A CONNECTION · STEADY RESPONSE & POLES

Do complex poles guarantee a displacement peak?
Close experiment

Separate two questions: free motion has no ongoing drive. Here F₀cos(Ωt) keeps driving the system; we examine only sinusoidal steady displacement after transients decay. Poles set transient modes; the drive Ω sets the steady oscillation frequency.

m x″ + b x′ + k x = F₀ cos(Ωt)

Fixed m=1kg, k=4N/m, F₀=1N, so natural angular frequency ω₀=√(k/m)=2rad/s. Damping ratio ζ=b/(2√(mk)) is dimensionless; viscous damping force is −b x′.

Free oscillation
Displacement peak
Steady gain & phase
Poles & transients

x_ss(t) = Re{X̂ eⁱΩᵗ}, G = kX̂/F₀ = 1/(1 − r² + i2ζr)
M = |G|, φ = arg G, r = Ω/ω₀

X̂ is a complex amplitude: it records size and phase. M=k|X̂|/F₀ is displacement amplitude relative to the static value F₀/k, with no units. It is not a band-pass output normalized to a peak of one.

Choose ζ=.2: the peak lies to the left of r=1. Then choose ζ=.8: poles are still complex, but the nonzero-frequency displacement peak is gone. Change only r: the probe moves, while poles stay fixed.

ω₀ comes from mass and spring. ωd is the underdamped free-transient frequency. Ω_peak identifies this displacement-gain peak. Ω is the applied drive. Changing Ω does not change system poles. Impulse response reveals transient modes; frequency response describes gain and phase after they decay. No startup process is simulated here.

Scope: ideal linear spring, viscous damping, ζ>0, causal fixed parameters. The steady formula is not a solution for undamped resonance. Velocity peaks, power absorption, nonlinearities and hardware are outside scope; different outputs can have different peaks.

nodes.title: Harmonic motion
nodes.description: An ideal spring has a restoring force proportional and opposite to displacement. Without damping or driving, its motion is sinusoidal.

nodes.title: Resonance
nodes.description: A periodically driven system may respond most strongly near a particular frequency. Damping changes the peak height and location.

nodes.title: Frequency response
nodes.description: For a stable LTI system, describe how a sinusoidal input’s amplitude and phase change in steady state, frequency by frequency.

nodes.title: Poles & stability
nodes.description: Poles describe exponential response modes. A causal continuous-time rational system is input-output stable when all transfer-function poles lie in the left half-plane.

nodes.title: Probability models
nodes.description: Use probabilities to describe possible outcomes and uncertainty. Model probabilities are distinct from observed evidence.

nodes.title: Bayesian updating
nodes.description: Combine a prior with the likelihood of an observation and normalize to obtain a posterior. The update depends on the observation model.

nodes.title: Kalman filtering
nodes.description: Predict a state with a dynamic model, then correct it using measurements and their uncertainty. Covariance describes model uncertainty, not guaranteed real-world error.

nodes.title: Feedback control
nodes.description: Measure an output, compare it with a target, and adjust the input. Results depend on the controller, system, delay and noise.
